articles.title: Roman lifts off on a mission to survey the infrared sky
articles.description:
Image:
			
NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA, at 07:26 EDT / 12:26 BST/ 13:26 CEST on 30 August 2026. With the successful launch, Roman began its mission to survey the sky in visible to near-infrared light to help reveal the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The telescope will also investigate the true diversity of exoplanets in our galaxy.
Roman is a NASA-led mission to which the European Space Agency (ESA) contributed star trackers, batteries, and detectors for the coronagraph instrument. ESA will also provide communications support through its deep-space ground station network, and enable data download using its new 35-metre antenna in New Norcia, Australia.
“I warmly congratulate our colleagues at NASA on the successful launch of Roman,” says Carole Mundell, ESA’s Director of Science. “ESA is proud to have provided essential hardware and to continue supporting Roman’s ambitious scientific goals. Together, we are opening new windows on the cosmos.”
Like ESA’s Euclid space telescope, Roman will enable astronomers to study the Universe in unprecedented detail. It is equipped with a primary mirror of 2.4 m and two instruments: the Wide Field Instrument (WFI) and a Coronagraph Instrument technology demonstration.
With its panoramic view of the sky, crisp infrared vision and quick re-orientation skills, Roman will perform fast and efficient surveys of a large area of the sky. By doing so, it will map clustering of galaxies over time and space and also study the light coming from thousands of distant type Ia supernovas which will help astronomers trace the expansion of the Universe.
“Roman should provide our clearest picture yet of whether dark energy is truly constant or whether it evolves over cosmic time – either outcome would have profound implications for our understanding of the Universe. I'm also excited by Roman's exoplanet census, which will discover thousands of new worlds, including cold planets and free-floating planets that have remained largely beyond our reach until now,” says Bethan James, ESA’s Roman Project Scientist. “Perhaps what excites me most is the unexpected. With its unprecedented combination of depth, area, and image quality, Roman has every opportunity to surprise us.”
After launch, Roman is on a steady course to the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2), nearly 1.5 million km away from Earth. This location allows the telescope to have an unobstructed view of a wide area of the sky, almost 12%. Like ESA’s Euclid and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope, Roman will move in a wider orbit around the L2 point – much larger than the Moon’s orbit around Earth.
In the next three months following launch, the Roman team will conduct a carefully orchestrated series of deployments, calibrations, and tests. Once the commissioning period is complete, the mission will begin its science operations, starting with the first science image release. Roman will spend at least five years scanning the infrared sky and is designed to work in space for another five years.
[Image description: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on board is seen transiting the Sun during launch from Launch Complex 39A, on Sunday 30 August 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, US.]
articles.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket to conduct a groundbreaking infrared survey of the universe.

articles.title: Watch live: BepiColombo begins its arrival at Mercury
articles.description:
After eight years, the ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission is about to enter its Mercury Arrival Phase. On 3 September 2026, ESA’s Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) will separate from BepiColombo’s two science orbiters – the first major step in one of the most operationally challenging planetary arrival sequences ever attempted by ESA.  
The European Space Agency (ESA) will livestream the critical milestone from 13:45 CEST. Tune in and witness the first step of one of the most complex phases of the mission, live from ESA mission control.  
Join ESA's livestream on YouTube here!
articles.summary: After eight years in transit, the ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission is beginning its arrival phase at Mercury on September 3, 2026. This landmark mission will study Mercury's geology, magnetic field, and atmospheric composition.

articles.title: eROSITA's Second Data Release Catalog Delivering the Most Comprehensive High-Energy Census of the Cosmos to Date
articles.description: The eROSITA Consortium has issued the survey's second data release (DR2), nearly doubling the previously known eROSITA X-ray sources to two million.
articles.summary: The eROSITA Consortium has released its second data release catalog, nearly doubling the X-ray sources known and providing the most comprehensive high-energy census of the cosmos to date. This major survey will enable unprecedented discoveries in high-energy astronomy.

articles.title: Scientists observe Einstein’s gravity in the quantum world for the first time
articles.description: Physicists have directly observed a long-predicted quantum effect of gravity, putting one of Einstein’s foundational ideas to a striking new test. Using ultracold atoms, researchers split an atom’s quantum wave so that one part was held in place while the other fell freely under gravity, then reunited the two to measure the tiny difference that emerged.
articles.summary: Physicists have directly observed a quantum effect of gravity predicted by Einstein, validating foundational ideas about how gravity operates at subatomic scales. This landmark experiment bridges quantum mechanics and general relativity.

articles.title: Dust and Water in Sagittarius A*
articles.description: A brilliant concentration of stars takes center stage in this Aug. 11, 2026, image taken by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. Webb observed IRS 3, a star near the end of its life cycle, located within this starfield. Webb’s mid-infrared data revealed the clear signature of oxygen-rich silicate dust, as well as, for the first […]
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a stunning image revealing dust and water structures around Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at our galaxy's center.

articles.title: BepiColombo begins Mercury arrival with MTM separation success
articles.description: On 3 September 2026 at 15:49 CEST, the European Space Agency's BepiColombo Mission Control Team at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) received the signal they had been waiting for – BepiColombo’s Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) successfully separated from the spacecraft stack. This landmark achievement for the ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) mission marks the first step of BepiColombo's long-awaited arrival at Mercury.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's BepiColombo mission successfully completes its Mercury Transfer Module separation, marking a crucial milestone in its journey to study Mercury.

articles.title: Unexplained Gamma-Rays from the Galactic Center Could be from Self-Annihilating Dark Matter
articles.description: Over a decade ago, the Fermi satellite detected an excess of gamma-ray emissions in the galactic center. Potential explanations included Sgr. A*, the Milky Way's SMBH, pulsars, and even self-annihilating dark matter. There's no clear answer yet, since the region is so difficult to observe. But recent research shows that dark matter can't be ruled out.
articles.summary: Gamma-ray emissions detected by the Fermi satellite in the galactic center over a decade ago may originate from self-annihilating dark matter particles. This finding could provide crucial evidence for understanding dark matter's fundamental nature.

articles.title: A New Surface Atlas of Phobos Will Help JAXA's MMX Mission Collect its Samples
articles.description: JAXA's Martian Moon eXploration (MMX) will be on its way to Mars and Phobos next month. It will collect samples from Phobos and return them to Earth. A new morphodynamic atlas of the small moon will help scientists collect and understand the samples.
articles.summary: JAXA's Martian Moon eXploration (MMX) mission will use a new surface atlas of Phobos to guide sample collection from Mars' enigmatic moon. This groundbreaking mission will unlock secrets about the Martian system's origins.

articles.title: New Revelations About the Origin of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.description: UK astronomers have uncovered new clues about the origin of 3I/Atlas – only the third known object from beyond our Solar System ever spotted in our cosmic neighbourhood.
articles.summary: UK astronomers have uncovered new clues about the origin of interstellar comet 3I/Atlas, only the third known object confirmed from beyond our Solar System. This discovery enhances our understanding of interstellar visitors and their journeys through space.

articles.title: New Research Says that Early Galaxies Could be Sending us Neutrinos
articles.description: Those "Little Red Dots" discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope, galaxies that existed during the very early Universe, could be sending neutrino particles that are reaching us today.
articles.summary: New research suggests that the earliest galaxies observed by the James Webb Space Telescope, known as 'Little Red Dots,' could be emitting neutrinos. This finding opens new avenues for studying the universe's earliest epochs.

articles.title: Continuous video of black hole radio observations challenges shock wave theory
articles.description: For years, scientists have relied primarily on radio imaging from techniques like very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) to study jets from the active galactic nuclei of supermassive black holes. This allows for the detection of broad, unresolved features, called components, moving at what appear to be faster-than-light speeds. However, traditional imaging has poor resolution and treats each observation as a separate snapshot in time, limiting information about how the features move.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Continuous video observations of black hole radio emissions challenge existing shock wave theory in accretion physics. This groundbreaking approach using advanced interferometry reveals new insights into black hole behavior.

articles.title: Scientists want to 3D print houses on Mars with the help of yeast
articles.description: Mars is a terrible place to build a house. It's bitterly cold, blasted by radiation and a near vacuum. Not to mention that the building materials, even for a modest shelter, could spend months hurtling through space before construction begins.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists are pioneering innovative 3D printing techniques using yeast-based materials to construct habitats on Mars. This breakthrough in Martian construction could revolutionize human settlement on the Red Planet.

articles.title: BepiColombo measures Mercury's particle bombardment up close
articles.description: The joint BepiColombo mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) is settling into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. In early September, BepiColombo's two orbiters, the Mercury Planetary Orbiter and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, separated from the transfer module. The orbiters will enter Mercury's orbit in November and separate from each other in December.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The BepiColombo mission has measured Mercury's particle bombardment environment up close, providing unprecedented data on the planet's interaction with the solar wind. These findings enhance understanding of planetary magnetospheres.

articles.title: Asteroid Ryugu's dust reveals nitrogen's slow concentration into complex molecules
articles.description: Nitrogen is a key ingredient in the biomolecules that form the building blocks of life. Yet as an unbonded gas, it is far more likely to drift into space than to lock itself into solid compounds, making it difficult for astronomers to trace its journey to Earth in the distant past.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of dust from asteroid Ryugu reveals how nitrogen slowly concentrates into complex organic molecules essential for life. This discovery illuminates the chemical processes that seed the building blocks of life throughout the cosmos.

articles.title: 'Fingerprints' inside the sun could reveal if it once swallowed a planet
articles.description: It is thought the sun may have engulfed a super-Earth-sized planet early in its history. Now, a new study has gone a step further, suggesting that such an event may have left behind detectable clues inside the sun that could still be visible today.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A new study uses 'fingerprints' within the Sun's composition to investigate whether it once engulfed a super-Earth-sized planet in its early history. This research provides insights into planetary system formation and evolution.

articles.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is bursting with methanol
articles.description: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS contains exceptionally high levels of methanol, suggesting it formed under conditions very different from those that shaped most comets in our solar system. ALMA also revealed that tiny icy grains around the comet are releasing methanol like miniature comets, giving astronomers an unusually detailed look at an object from another star system.
articles.summary: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS contains exceptionally high levels of methanol, suggesting it formed under unique conditions in a distant stellar system. This composition offers clues about planetary formation in other star systems.

articles.title: Astronomers detect ancient hydrogen signal that could help map the Universe
articles.description: Astronomers have detected an exceptionally faint hydrogen radio signal from billions of light-years away using South Africa’s MeerKAT telescope. Instead of finding galaxies one at a time, the technique measures their combined hydrogen glow across enormous stretches of space. The successful detection shows that astronomers may soon be able to create much larger 3D maps of the Universe.
articles.summary: Astronomers have detected an exceptionally faint ancient hydrogen radio signal from billions of light-years away using advanced instrumentation. This achievement opens new possibilities for mapping the universe's large-scale structure.

articles.title: NASA scientists discover a giant 10-sided pattern on Saturn
articles.description: A huge 10-sided atmospheric pattern has appeared around Saturn’s south pole, giving the planet a surprising counterpart to its famous northern hexagon. Hubble data suggest the strange decagon only began emerging in the past few years and is still growing stronger. Researchers hope continued observations will reveal why it suddenly formed and whether it could persist for decades.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a massive 10-sided atmospheric pattern around Saturn's south pole, revealing surprising complexity in the gas giant's weather systems. This geometric phenomenon offers new insights into planetary atmospheric dynamics.

articles.title: Scientists study 3,000 supernovas and discover that dark energy may be evolving
articles.description: A catalog of almost 3,000 white dwarfs that exploded as type Ia supernovas after overfeeding on companion stars indicates that dark energy is changing over time.
articles.summary: Analysis of nearly 3,000 Type Ia supernovae indicates that dark energy may be evolving rather than remaining constant over cosmic time. This discovery could reshape our understanding of the universe's long-term fate.

articles.title: Four amateur astronomers using a telescope in Chile’s Atacama desert found a comet on 13 January 2026, 81 days before it would graze past the Sun. Nobody alive had seen its previous pass, because the orbit it travels on brings it back only about every 1,900 years.
articles.description:
A glimpse of a celestial wanderer that last visited during the Middle Ages—caught not by professional observatories, but by four amateurs with a telescope and patience.
The post Four amateur astronomers using a telescope in Chile’s Atacama desert found a come…
articles.summary: Amateur astronomers in Chile's Atacama Desert discovered a rare comet that hasn't been seen since the Middle Ages, demonstrating how citizen scientists continue to make significant astronomical discoveries.

articles.title: Icy Exocomets Around a Distant Star Help Explain Earth's Water
articles.description: Did icy comets deliver water to the young Earth? That idea won't go away. Now, astronomers at Lund University in Sweden have found evidence of exocomets orbiting a young star named PDS 70. The observations suggest that these comets are delivering water to tha…
articles.summary: Swedish astronomers studying icy exocomets around a distant star provide new evidence supporting the theory that cometary impacts delivered water to early Earth.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Discover Giant 10-Sided Pattern on Saturn’s South Pole
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has detected a massive, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave circling Saturn’s south pole, according to a study published Sept. 3, 2026, in the journal Science Advances. The finding, reported by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, …
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has detected an extraordinary 10-sided atmospheric wave circling Saturn's south pole, offering scientists a rare opportunity to study the evolution of unusual planetary phenomena.

articles.title: Is it a planet or a moon? Scientists discover a strange Jupiter-sized world orbiting a brown dwarf in a never-before-seen cosmic system
articles.description: Astronomers found a massive object orbiting a brown dwarf star. This discovery challenges existing definitions of planets and moons. The unusual system features a nested orbital arrangement unlike our solar system. Scientists are debating the object's classif…
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a massive Jupiter-sized object orbiting a brown dwarf in an unprecedented cosmic system, challenging and expanding our understanding of planetary formation and classification.

articles.title: Astronomers Hear the Faint Whispers of Cosmic Hydrogen from the Distant Past.
articles.description: Astronomers have directly detected an extremely faint radio signal from hydrogen gas billions of light years away, demonstrating a powerful new way to map the Universe.
articles.summary: Astronomers have directly detected faint radio signals from hydrogen gas billions of light-years away, opening new windows into the distant cosmic past.

articles.title: Astronomers already knew the Milky Way’s magnetic field reverses near the Sagittarius Arm, but a new 2026 three-dimensional model revealed the boundary’s unexpected shape: not a vertical wall between spiral arms, but a tilted magnetic plane slicing diagonally through the Galactic disc and passing just above our own region of space.
articles.description:
A 2026 model replaces the familiar vertical boundary near the Sagittarius Arm with a tilted magnetic plane passing above the Sun in Galactic coordinates.
The post Astronomers already knew the Milky Way’s magnetic field reverses near the Sagittarius Arm, but a…
articles.summary: A 2026 three-dimensional model reveals that the Milky Way's magnetic field boundary near the Sagittarius Arm forms a tilted plane rather than a vertical wall, reshaping our understanding of galactic structure.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Djibouti Artemis Accords Signing Ceremony
articles.description: The Republic of Djibouti will sign the Artemis Accords during a ceremony at 11 a.m. EDT, Monday, Sept. 14, at NASA Headquarters in Washington, becoming the 72nd country signatory. NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson will host Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States Mohamed Siad Douale for the ceremony, together with U.S. State Department Assistant […]
articles.summary: The Republic of Djibouti signs the Artemis Accords, joining the international commitment to peaceful space exploration and lunar cooperation.

articles.title: NASA Answers President’s Call to Establish United States Space Academy
articles.description: Less than two weeks after an Executive Order was signed to create the first United States Space Academy, NASA-led work is in full swing to make the academy a reality and shape the future of America’s aerospace workforce and leadership. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman chaired the first Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy […]
articles.summary: NASA leads efforts to establish the first United States Space Academy, advancing education and training for the next generation of space professionals.

articles.title: NASA’s Life-Saving Technology Where Cell Signals Can’t Go
articles.description: Search and rescue technology developed in part by NASA saved five lives
articles.summary: NASA-developed search and rescue technology saves five lives, demonstrating the life-saving applications of space innovation.

articles.title: NASA Adds Relativity Space’s Terran R to Launch Services Contract
articles.description: A NASA Launch Services (NLS) II contract has been awarded by the agency to Relativity Space Inc., and its Terran R launch service in accordance with the contract’s on-ramp provision. The Terran R launch service will be available to NASA’s launch services to use for future missions. The NLS II contracts are multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts […]
articles.summary: NASA awards Relativity Space's Terran R rocket to its Launch Services II contract, expanding commercial launch capabilities for space missions.

articles.title: BepiColombo’s Mercury arrival begins - full replay
articles.description:
Video: 
			02:31:10
				
Watch the replay of the livestream originally broadcast on 3 September as ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission took the first critical step towards arriving at Mercury.
After travelling through the inner Solar System together for eight years, BepiColombo's Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) will separate from the rest of the stacked spacecraft on 3 September 2026. This marks the beginning of one of the most complex planetary arrival sequences ever attempted by ESA.
Broadcast live from ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, the programme includes live views from the iconic Main Control Room, expert analysis, behind-the-scenes insights, and the first signal from the spacecraft following separation. 
Livestream schedule (CEST): 

13:45 – Livestream begins 
16:00-16:45 – End of livestream
articles.summary: ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission livestream replay documents the historic arrival operations at Mercury.
